merge.title: Fault response without attempt-charging: zeroize-then-reset in the glitch-halt sink, a written verdict-vs-availability rule, sparse phase words, PIN-scrambler RNG fail-closed, and diagnostics-only SE fault counting
merge.threat:
An attacker holding the device runs repeated glitch trials. The live gap is not "trials are free" (that part is already bounded, see below) but that the one remaining non-zeroizing park keeps secrets resident.

- **Halt with secrets resident.** `pqsigner_fi::halt_on_glitch` is a bare `wfe` loop, reached from both invariant checks in `wait_random_loop`, which runs thousands of times per signature. If it trips inside an unlocked gateway handler, `master_secret`, `slot_master_entropy` and the cached slot SigningKey stay in S-SRAM with the core parked. The SysTick idle wipe is suppressed while `handler_is_busy()`, and the watchdog keeps being fed on handler-busy for up to `MAX_BUSY_TICKS` = 30,000 ticks (~30 s) plus the ~2 s IWDG period.
- **Stack copies survive the reset.** Boot only calls `zeroize_sensitive_state()` (statics and SE caches) on watchdog/software/low-power resets, so handler stack-local secret copies are not scrubbed.
- **Dense phase encodings.** First-boot and journal step words are dense u8, so a single flipped value is another valid phase.
- **PIN scrambler fails open.** On an RNG error the F-20 start digits silently fall back to all-zero.

What is NOT a live threat: glitch trials against the PIN gate are already charged (page-124 precharge before every SE call), and confirmed-fault sites in signing already relock after one trip.
merge.proposal:
One firmware item with five parts and no new flash state. Nothing here charges a PIN attempt on a detected fault.

**(A) Halt sink zeroizes, then resets — P1, cost S.**
- `halt_on_glitch` lives in the pure-logic `pqsigner-fi` crate shared with the FSBL, so it needs a registered hook (same pattern as the `pqsigner_sha256_*` extern hooks).
- Secure world binds the hook to: mask interrupts, `nsc::zeroize_sensitive_state()`, `fi::zeroize_barrier()`, scrub the secure stack region below the current SP (or switch to a fresh stack first), then `SCB::sys_reset()`. This matches the existing HardFault handler (rr-1) and `hash_engine_fault` (H-1).
- FSBL binds a bare halt (it holds no secrets).
- No display or SE I/O in the hook (#484 rule). No TAMP BKERASE.
- Extend the boot scrub (`requires_secret_scrub`) to fill the secure stack/unused SRAM, not only the named statics, so IWDG and NRST exits are covered too.
- Must be safe from exception context: the consumption-mask SysTick reseed reaches `wait_random`.

**(B) Write the classification rule down and pin it with a source-invariant test — cost S.**
- CONFIRMED-fault sites (the `c10_sign_verified` ct_eq mismatch, CfiCounter mismatch, verify gate) relock via `zeroize_sensitive_state`. This is already implemented.
- AVAILABILITY sites (TRNG SECS/CECS, pool contention, SE transport/no-verdict, parse rejects) refuse the operation and never write page 124 beyond the existing `gated_unlock` precharge.
- No site outside `gated_unlock` calls `pin_attempts_bump`. No `in_progress ⇒ wipe` rule.
- Land the #835 option-2 commits on master first; they are on `perf/flash-opt-level-z` only.

**(C) Sparse Hamming-distant u32 phase words — cost S.**
- Apply to `FirstBootStep` and the journal `STEP_*` constants, with `default ⇒ fail-closed`.
- `crypto.rs` CFI steps are already sparse. `fw_update` has no phase enum, so only add one if a state word is introduced.
- Journal `STEP_*` is a persisted format on page 127: change it only before any unit runs first boot.

**(D) PIN-entry scrambler fails closed — cost S, owner confirmation needed.**
- `pin_entry::enter_pin` discards the `rng_strong::fill` result and falls back to zero starts.
- Change it to: one bounded retry, then refuse with an RNG-error screen. No attempt charged, no wipe.
- This reverses a rationale recorded in the code comment, in line with the owner's 2026-10-09 "if the RNG fails, error out" (#834).

**(E) Diagnostics only, no escalation — cost S.**
- Add `AttemptReason` codes that split `NoVerdict` into transport / FI-gate / SE-status.
- Keep per-session SRAM counters of SE050 WTX/read-retry exhaustion and OPTIGA re-init, readable through the existing attempt-log path (subject to #719).
- This is the data needed to root-cause #715 and #692 before anyone revisits escalation.

**Deferred to an explicit owner decision — not recommended now.**
- A durable fault tally that a correct PIN does NOT reset, with admin wipe at N. This is the only escalation shape that survives the re-unlock bypass. It needs new flash state, a tear-resistant precharge shape, and the #715/#692/#109 root causes closed first.
- Softening the single `CounterUnstable` read that today ends in a full dual-SE wipe.

No round-1 verification; verified here. (2) SRAM tally of N trips => lock: dropped, because one confirmed trip already relocks and non-confirmed check_true failures are ordinary input rejections. dropped_parts: Charge page 124 on sentinel/CFI/receipt trips outside gated_unlock (FI-05 part 1, SYS-04 part 1). pin_attempts_bump is MCU page 124 only and reconcile never advances E120 or the SE050 UserID, so it is not three-way (invariant #2 forbids that claim). Post-unlock the charge is reset by the next correct PIN; pre-unlock, gated_unlock already precharges. It also re-creates #835 C3, rejected by both reviewers and by the owner's option-2 decision.

in_progress / second-trip => dual-SE admin wipe or page-125 arm (FI-05 part 1, pin-10 b). wait_random is reachable from the SysTick consumption-mask reseed and from NS-preempted veneers (#835 C1/H5), so re-entry is a scheduling event and would give compromised NS a wipe primitive. It also contradicts the recorded HardFault design note (main.rs:4669-4675: no SE wipe on induced faults, reserved for confirmed TAMP/GTZC).
pin-10 (a) 'verdict-class trip charges exactly one attempt' inside the PIN gate: already implemented by the precharge plus the NoVerdict keep-charged arms.

Routing SCP03/CCM receipt failures, read_volatile_voted CounterUnstable, and SE retry-exhaustion into charge or lock (FI-05, SYS-04 part 3 escalation half). These fire with no attacker on pq1 silicon (#715, #692, #109).
SYS-04 part 2, session tally N=3 => lock + zeroize + reset: redundant, since confirmed-fault sites relock after one trip (crypto.rs:373-389).

SYS-04 part 4, persistent option-byte (tz-1) mismatch arms the page-125 wipe. The FSBL is pre-PIN with no SE or page-125 write path; adding one costs FSBL flash against the 32 KiB linker region and puts a runtime flash write in the trust root. After RDP-2 the option bytes are frozen, so a mismatch is a read glitch or pre-lock state and a wipe is a pure DoS. FSBL halt (fsbl/src/main.rs:244-252) stays. Trezor's secret_safety_erase precedent is real but protects a flash-resident secret pq1 does not have.

SYS-04 part 5, feeding HardFault/NMI reset clusters into a tally (depends on SYS-06, which is outside this cluster): needs persisted state that CLAUDE.md's flash-state restrictions discourage, and is tearable.

TAMP BKERASE of the BHK registers at halt (FI-05 part 2). No BKERASE exists in secure/src; the BHK is reloaded from DHUK-wrapped page 126 each boot, so it is not a cryptographic erase, and it touches the BHK/SE050 axis the owner decided to keep (#707, #712 lifecycle bug first).
Zeroize then stay parked in wfe (the literal FI-05/pin-10 wording): replaced by zeroize-then-reset to match rr-1 and H-1. A masked-IRQ park would only be exited by the IWDG ~2 s later anyway.
SYS-04 novelty 'beyond': Trezor ships the pattern.
Donjon/Tangem cited as support for charge-on-fault (FI-05): that source shows a post-detection fault counter being defeated by power tearing.

merge.precedent:
Trezor ships every kept part.

- **Halt/reboot clears RAM.** `core/embed/sys/startup/stm32/bootutils.c:103-198` (halt_device / reboot_with_args_phase_2 fill all runtime RAM) through `call_with_new_stack` in `sysutils.c:31-79` (fresh stack, CPSID F, BKERASE).
- **Generic fault checks do not charge.** `ensure()` → `__fatal_error` → RSOD → halt/reboot with no counter charge (`rtl/error_handling.h:144-149`).
- **Sparse result words with fatal default.** `bootloader/workflow/workflow_common.h:23-33` (WF_ERROR_FATAL = 0, `default:` falls into it); `secbool` 0xAAAAAAAA.
- **The charge-on-fault ladder is storage-only.** `storage/storage.c:1815-1844` `__handle_fault` (verified: in_progress ⇒ storage_wipe; increment the PIN-fail counter and require ctr+1) is used only inside storage.c and charges only the MCU norcow counter. pq1's equivalent is the `gated_unlock` precharge, already present (same shape as Trezor `storage.c:1210-1221`).
- **Bootloader fatal erase.** `bootloader/main.c:677-690` (WF_ERROR_FATAL ⇒ secret_bhk_regenerate + erase_storage) and `boardloader/main.c:325-332` (option-byte configure failure ⇒ secret_safety_erase) are real, but they protect flash-resident secrets pq1 does not hold.

Ledger publishes no post-detection policy. Tangem's persistent fault counter was defeated by power tearing (Donjon). In-repo precedent for zeroize-then-reset: the HardFault handler (rr-1) and `hash_engine_fault` (H-1).

live_defects.what: halt_on_glitch parks in a bare wfe loop without zeroizing. When it trips inside an unlocked gateway handler, master_secret, slot_master_entropy and the cached slot SigningKey stay in S-SRAM with the core stopped.
live_defects.evidence: pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs:273-285 (bare loop { wfe() }), callers :144 and :153 in wait_random_loop. secure/src/main.rs:4350 gates the idle wipe on !nsc::handler_is_busy(). secure/src/hw/iwdg.rs:137 and :287-303 keep feeding the watchdog on handler-busy for MAX_BUSY_TICKS = 30,000 ticks. HardFault (main.rs:4680-4692) and panic (:4711-4713) both zeroize, so this is the only non-zeroizing park. Identical on master, origin/master and perf/flash-opt-level-z (:263).
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes. PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718) includes iwdg and consumption-mask, and wait_random runs throughout signing and unlock. Residency is bounded, not indefinite: about 30 s of busy-feed plus the ~2 s IWDG period, then a watchdog reset whose boot scrub (main.rs:1332) clears the named statics. If the trip is in SysTick context the feed stops at once (~2 s). Not exercised on silicon here; mode-production itself is currently unbuildable behind the S-2 fence.
live_defects.severity: medium-high: a multi-second window with live secrets and a parked core, on a path that fires exactly when a glitch has been detected

live_defects.what: Handler stack-local secret copies are not scrubbed on any halt or abnormal-reset path. zeroize_sensitive_state clears SecureState and SE caches only, and the boot scrub calls the same function.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1729-1745 (with_state zeroize_sensitive + SE.zeroize_caches, no stack fill); secure/src/main.rs:1311-1333 (boot scrub = zeroize_sensitive_state); main.rs:4344-4348 comment states handlers hold stack-local copies of master_secret/entropy/slot_master_entropy. Trezor fills all runtime RAM (bootutils.c:103-198).
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes by construction for any IWDG, software or HardFault reset taken mid-handler. Whether a given secret is still on the stack at that moment depends on the frame layout; not measured.

live_defects.what: The PIN-entry digit scrambler (F-20) silently degrades to all-zero start digits when rng_strong::fill fails; the Result is discarded.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:73-88 (`let _ = crate::rng_strong::fill(&mut rand_bytes);` with a documented fallback to start-at-0). Same text on perf/flash-opt-level-z.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes whenever rng_strong::fill returns Err. Under e2e-test, enter_pin is short-circuited, so bench images do not exercise it. Impact is limited to losing the press-count shoulder-surf defence; an attacker able to force the RNG failure regains that channel.

live_defects.what: A single disagreeing pair of page-124 reads in gated_unlock returns PinLocked, which the caller converts into a full dual-SE factory reset.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1429-1436 (CounterUnstable -> Err(PinLocked)); secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:160-164 (PinLocked -> trigger_lockout_wipe); also cmd_request_unlock.rs:117-125 on the PinIncorrect arm.

This is deliberate fail-closed (FAIL-IN) design, not a bug: the wallet is recoverable from the 24 words and an attacker with the device can already force a wipe with 10 wrong PINs. Listed because it is the one place where a single transient event destroys SE state, the opposite of the #835 principle. Owner decision, not a fix.

live_defects.what: First-boot phase encodings are dense small integers, so a single flipped value is another valid step.

merge.residual_after:
- **Glitch trials stay free in attempt terms.** Each detected trip costs the attacker one reset (and, post-unlock, one PIN re-entry), not a durable counter. Nothing durable is charged outside the PIN gate.
- **PIN-holding attackers are unbounded.** Someone who knows the PIN, or an evil-maid setup where the owner keeps unlocking, can run unlimited trials against the signing path. The only defences are double-compute + ct_eq + verify-before-release and the relock.
- **The pre-reset window remains.** A fault that skips the hook call, or corrupts it before zeroize completes, still leaves secrets resident. The backstop is the IWDG plus the boot scrub, and the ~30 s handler-busy feed window still applies in that case.
- **Cold reset skips the scrub.** A BOR/NRST reset classified `Cold` is not scrubbed at boot, so a fast power-cycle or cold-boot read of SRAM retention is not covered. With no battery this rests on decay time.
- **Undetected faults are untouched.** Identical deterministic faults in both signing passes, faults inside the SE, and data faults that land on valid sentinel values all escape detection.
- **The PIN budget is still MCU-led.** Page 124 remains the only pre-verdict charge. The silicon backstops are E120 (32 lifetime attempts) and the SE050 UserID, which advance only on real SE verifies. A tear between the page-124 bump and the SE call is the accepted MCU-lead state.
- **SE-fault masking remains.** A persistent SE fault can still drain the 10-attempt budget (#692, #715, #109), and silent SE050 retry loops still mask fault attempts on the bus. Part (E) only makes them visible.
- **The FSBL is unchanged.** Its halt stays bare and a persistent option-byte mismatch only halts.
merge.rationale:
**Why the charge-on-fault half is dropped.** All three members propose it; round 1 refuted it for FI-05 and the same reasons hold for the other two.
- `pin_attempts_bump` charges MCU page 124 only.
- A post-unlock charge is erased by the next correct PIN, so it bounds no one.
- Pre-unlock trials are already precharged.
- The trigger set fires benignly on pq1 silicon (#715, #692, #109).
- The owner has already chosen "failed operation, not halt or burn" in #835.

**What survives.** The parts with no policy content, each backed by a defect I confirmed in the executing code:
- the bare-`wfe` halt with secrets live (bounded to roughly 32 s in the production feature set by the watchdog, not indefinite as the members claim);
- unscrubbed handler stack copies;
- the scrambler's fail-open RNG fallback;
- dense first-boot phase words.

**Why reset rather than park.** The repo already made that call twice (rr-1 HardFault handler, H-1 `hash_engine_fault`), so the hook follows suit.

**Priority.** P1 overall because part (A) is cheap and closes the only non-zeroizing park; parts (C)–(E) are P2.

**Not verified.** The advisor tool was rate-limited, so this reconciliation had no second-model check. Nothing was built or run on silicon; all evidence is from reading source on `feat/pq1-board-target` and three other refs.

skeptic.reason:
The core holds: dropping every charge-on-fault / second-trip-wipe variant is correct and consistent with the code and with the #835 owner decision, and the central defect (a non-zeroizing glitch park) is real on HEAD. But three parts need fixing before this is actionable.

(1) BYPASS / part (A). The hook as written does not clear the material that is actually live. Handlers hold stack-local copies of master_secret/entropy (main.rs:4344-4348), and those frames sit ABOVE the current SP; the proposal says to scrub "below the current SP", which is dead stack only. zeroize_sensitive_state (nsc/mod.rs:1729-1745) clears statics + SE caches, so zeroize-then-reset leaves the caller-frame copies in SRAM1 across the reset exactly as the IWDG path does today. The real closure for that is the already-tracked option byte SRAM_RST=0 (#82, OPEN, priority:high), which the merge missed entirely. With #82, the hook reduces to mask-IRQs + zeroize + barrier + sys_reset, and both stack-scrub sub-items become fallback only.

(2) Part (C) is mis-targeted. FirstBootStep is only a fault-screen/UI label (state.rs:220-273, number() for the "X/N" line); it never drives a transition. Persisted STEP_* records carry MAGIC + CRC32 over bytes 0..12 (journal.rs:125-136) and scan accepts only 1..=STEP_MAX (journal.rs:221), so a flipped stored id fails CRC rather than becoming another valid step. The real control word is the one-hot `done` bitmask, consumed by bare `if done & DONE_X == 0` branches (state.rs:306/323/333/345/375) with no check_true — sparse step encodings do not touch that.

(3) Feasibility/sequencing. Making the #835 perf-branch merge a prerequisite for (A) is unnecessary: halt_on_glitch and its two callers are identical on HEAD and perf/flash-opt-level-z, so the hook is independent of the RNG path.

Residual after the corrected item: each detected trip costs the attacker one reset plus (post-unlock) one PIN entry, nothing durable; a fault that skips the hook call falls back to IWDG; undetected faults are untouched. Real-world gain of (A) is modest: while parked the core executes only the secure SysTick, RDP-2 removes debug, and NS cannot read S-SRAM, so the window needs a second physical capability to exploit.
skeptic.corrections:
PART (A)
- Add #82 (SRAM_RST=0) as the primary fix for "stack copies survive reset" and for the Cold/NRST residual. Constraint the merge does not state: RDP-2 freezes option bytes, so SRAM_RST must be staged before the Phase-A burn, and the first-boot ship-profile check does not verify it today (no SRAM_RST reference anywhere in secure/src/first_boot/). Verify in RM0456 + on silicon (the #82 canary test) that SRAM_RST covers SRAM1 at 0x3000_0000 for IWDG and SYSRESETREQ resets; I did not check the reference manual.
- Fix the stack-scrub direction: live secrets are in caller frames ABOVE SP. If a software scrub is kept as fallback it must wipe the whole stack up to _stack_start (192K RAM, secure/memory-stm32u585*.x) from a register-only routine or after a stack switch (Trezor call_with_new_stack). There is no stack-bottom linker symbol today.
- Mechanism: do not add an extern hook. wait_random_loop already takes its RNG as a closure and check_true takes `wait`; pass the halt action the same way (an `on_glitch` diverging closure / fn pointer). No new unsafe in pqsigner-fi; FSBL passes a bare wfe loop.
- Exception-context safety is fine: with_state is an unlocked raw &mut (nsc/state.rs:589-594), so there is no deadlock; HardFault and NMI already do the same.
- SysTick does reach wait_random on HEAD (consumption_mask.rs:181-183 -> rng::fill -> hw/rng.rs:173.. wait_random), so the ISR claim is correct.
- Decouple from the #835 merge; it is not a prerequisite for (A).
- Residency bound: ~30 s busy-feed + ~2 s IWDG confirmed for a thread-mode trip in a handler (iwdg.rs:126-137, 276-303; RLR 250 / div 256). Not closed: under ui-px (non-shipping) the TrustedUiWaitGuard spans the whole navigation phase (ui/px/lcd.rs:750), so if a thread-mode wait_random is reachable there the IWDG is fed until the 120 s idle limit, then another 30 s. In the legacy confirm the guard wraps only wait_button (confirm.rs:194) and I found no wait_random under it. State the bound as "~32 s in the shipping UI; longer under ui-px, untraced".
- "The only non-zeroizing park" is slightly too strong: flash.rs:581-590 obl_launch parks in wfe (first-boot only, no wallet secrets), and sign_rate.rs:385-390 spins in wfi on a voted-read disagreement inside a handler (recovers, but relies on the 30 s busy cap).

PART (B)
- "gated_unlock is the only production pin_attempts_bump caller" is true only modulo cfg: cmd_test_pin_lockout.rs:158 (e2e-only) and main.rs:3253-3254 (under #[cfg(feature = "pin-gate-hw-counter-e2e")] at :3116) also call it. The source-invariant test must allowlist those by feature gate. Existing pins already assert the precharge (nsc_core_under_test/pure_tests.rs:448-452, nsc_small_cmds_pure_tests.rs:1456).

PART (C)
- Drop "sparse FirstBootStep / STEP_*". Either drop (C) or reframe it as: route the `done & DONE_*` skip gates (state.rs:306-375) through check_true_into_sentinel and re-scan the journal before committing STEP_ALL_DONE. A single skipped branch there skips an SE050/OPTIGA transport->final rotation, which invariant #3 calls load-bearing. This is production-only (rdp2-self-lock) candidate code with other open gates, so P2/P3.

PART (D)
- Defect confirmed (pin_entry.rs:73-88). Still needs owner confirmation because the code comment records the opposite rationale. rng_strong::fill includes SE GetRandom, so refusing turns SE transport flake (#715/#692 class) into "no PIN screen"; enter_pin is also reached from the PendSV re-unlock, so the refusal path must not feed the #692 retry loop.

LIVE DEFECTS
1. halt_on_glitch bare wfe: CONFIRMED (pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs:273-281, callers :144/:153; identical on perf/flash-opt-level-z :263). Severity is medium at most, not medium-high.
2. Stack copies not scrubbed: CONFIRMED by construction (boot scrub main.rs:1330-1333 = zeroize_sensitive_state only), but ALREADY TRACKED as #82; not untracked.
3. PIN scrambler fail-open: CONFIRMED, low.
4. CounterUnstable -> PinLocked -> trigger_lockout_wipe: CONFIRMED (nsc/mod.rs:1428-1437; cmd_request_unlock.rs:117-125, 160-164). Deliberate design; owner decision only.
5. Dense first-boot phase words: DENIED as stated (label enum + CRC-framed records). Replace with the unhardened `done` gates above.

OTHER
- #835's "H4 closed ... there is no wfe loop" is false for pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs:274; confirmed, keep as untracked-delta item 7.
- Trezor precedent verified: random_delays.c:193,200 -> error_shutdown("(glitch)"); bootutils.c:105-158 clear_unused_stack + memregion_fill via call_with_new_stack; storage.c:1815-1844 __handle_fault as quoted.
- Priority: P2 rather than P1. (A) is hygiene parity with rr-1; the durable fix for retained material is #82, which is already priority:high.
- Kind becomes mixed (firmware + option-byte provisioning). Cost S for (A) alone, M for the bundle.
- Nothing was built or run; all findings are from reading source on feat/pq1-board-target and perf/flash-opt-level-z. The codex MCP reviewer was unavailable (connection closed).
